newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson sees 1996 orders at 130 bln SKR.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson sees 1996 orders at 130 bln SKR.

text.p: Swedish telecoms giant LM Ericsson AB said on Tuesday that it expected to end 1996 on a strong note, expecting order bookings to reach about 130 billion crowns for the full year.
"The order bookings this year will be about 130 billion crowns or more," Ericsson's chief executive Lars Ramqvist told a press conference.
"We now have about 10 billion crowns or more in order bookings each month."
On Tuesday Ericsson posted a 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits for the first nine months of 1996 to 6.26 billion crowns and a 22 percent rise in order bookings to 95.63 billion crowns.
Ramqvist said he extrapolated the year's figure from the nine month result.
The company's finance director CW Ros was also positive about order bookings.
"We have built up our order stocks and it is looking good for the coming period," Ros told the press conference.

"We have tougher competition on the market (for mobile telephones) but it is a bit less tough than we believed it would be a year ago. On the systems side, it continues to be hard and that is why we see some lower margins," he said

In its nine month report the company sounded a warning bell about increasing competition and greater financial exposure, saying gross margins weakened slightly in the first three quarters of the year.
